title: Dual-Use Risk — Cyber, Bio, Chem, Nuclear Uplift

questions.question: What does the local DOMAINS table identify as the remaining nuclear bottleneck?
options: A lack of language-model context windows
A missing watermark detector
Fissile-material acquisition, which is not solved by more information alone
The absence of any nuclear physics data
questions.explanation: The nuclear row stays limited in both 2024 and 2025 and names material access as the bottleneck. That is different from bio/chem/cyber, where the lesson describes information or execution gains.

questions.question: What did the cited Anthropic cyber case report for agentic coding?
options: No automation beyond code completion
A complete ban on all defensive security use
A result limited to model watermarking
80–90% of a campaign automated, with humans intervening in only 4–6 steps
questions.explanation: The lesson treats agentic coding as the inflection: reconnaissance, exploitation, post-exploitation, and exfiltration can be connected into a workflow. The remaining four-to-six human steps are a bottleneck, not proof of harmlessness.

questions.question: What is the chem/bio execution-gap erosion described in the lesson?
options: Vision-enabled models watch wet-lab video and provide real-time protocol correction
Models replace every wet-lab instrument with a simulation
Models only summarize old protocols and cannot observe experiments
Models remove the need for precursor or pathogen procurement
questions.explanation: The execution gap narrows when a model can see an experiment and flag a procedural error while work is underway. Equipment and precursor procurement remain non-informational constraints.

questions.question: What novice-relative uplift figure is cited for the 2025 bio trial?
options: 0.25x, the random multiple-choice baseline
2.53x, which was insufficient to rule out ASL-3
79x, the wet-lab efficiency demonstration
80–90%, the cyber campaign estimate
80–90%, the cyber campaign estimate
questions.explanation: 2.53x compares novice performance with and without the model in the cited bio acquisition task. The 79x figure belongs to the wet-lab protocol-optimization demonstration, so the two numbers answer different questions.

questions.question: Why does the lesson distinguish novice-relative from expert-absolute capability?
options: The two measures are synonyms with different units
Expert capability is always lower because experts ignore model output
Novice-relative uplift measures only hardware access
A model can give novices a large multiplicative uplift while an expert extracts a much higher absolute capability ceiling
questions.explanation: Novice-relative uplift compares against a status-quo baseline; expert-absolute capability asks what a motivated expert can elicit and execute. A safety case that addresses only novice prompts can miss expert elicitation.

questions.question: What follows for a safety case from this novice/expert asymmetry?
options: Input refusals alone are sufficient once novice uplift is measured
Only model size matters; capability decomposition is unnecessary
Material bottlenecks prove that no cyber or bio evaluation is needed
The case should add elicitation-hardening, capability or access controls, and control/monitoring evidence for expert use
questions.explanation: The lesson recommends controls that address both how capability is elicited and what happens when an expert can use it. Monitoring, illegibility, and incapability are complementary safety-case pillars, not substitutes for domain evidence.
